title: Sales Enablement: Enterprise GTM Kit — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:
This Enterprise GTM Kit equips reps and AE teams to position Redwood Inference with enterprise prospects, win competitive deals, and accelerate procurement. The document includes: concise positioning and messaging, competitive brief and battlecards, a recommended pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, two anonymized case studies with measurable outcomes, a prospect-facing Security FAQ, and a step-by-step POC/closing playbook.

TL;DR Positioning (1‑liner + elevator):
- 1‑liner: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, cost‑efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Elevator (30s): For engineering teams that need production-grade LLM inference, Redwood provides a unified runtime, predictable pricing, and enterprise controls—so teams get fast time-to-value without building or operating their own inference stack.

Primary Personas and Buying Committee:
- Primary users: ML Engineers, Software Engineers (Platform/Backend), ML Platform leads.
- Influencers: Security/Trust, Infra/Cloud Architects, Data Privacy, App/Product Managers.
- Economic buyer: VP/Head of Engineering, Platform, or CTO.

Core Value Props (short bullets per persona):
- Platform/Engineers: Low-latency, high-throughput serving with measurable SLOs, autoscaling, and predictable cost controls.
- ML/Applied ML: Model lifecycle support, evals integration, quantization suggestions, and verified performance profiles.
- Security/IT: Private deployments, VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and SOC2-compliant controls.
- Product/PM: Faster time-to-market, consistent dev experience across environments, and lower infra overhead.

Messaging Pillars (talking points):
1) Production-grade inference: emphasize throughput, latency SLOs, KV/prefix caching, and predictable unit economics.
2) Unified deployment modes: same API and control plane for hosted, dedicated, or private—reduces integration work.
3) Cost control levers: batching, caching, quantization profiles with measurable token cost improvements.
4) Reliability & graceful degradation: automated fallbacks, model variants, and regional routing to maintain SLAs.
5) Enterprise controls: audit logs, RBAC, KMS integration, and contractual SLAs for Dedicated/Private.

Competitive Brief (summary + win themes):
- Competitors to watch: Hyperscaler managed endpoints (e.g., CloudAI endpoints), LLM API providers, and self‑managed inference runtimes.
- Typical strengths of competitors: deep cloud integration (hyperscalers), low initial friction for small workloads, or customizability for self-hosted solutions.
- Redwood win themes: predictable unit economics at scale, unified tooling across environments, rapid onboarding via developer SDKs, and enterprise-grade private deployment options.

Battlecard — Common Objections & Rebuttals:
- Objection: "We can run this cheaper ourselves."
  - Rebuttal: Running at production scale hides many operational costs (eviction risk, kernel optimization, batching tuning, and on-call overhead). We provide measurable per-token cost comparisons and recommendations (batching/quant) that usually reduce total cost of ownership vs. DIY. Offer a pilot with telemetry to demonstrate.
- Objection: "We need strict data residency / air‑gapped options."
  - Rebuttal: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem deployments and customer-managed KMS; we have an established on‑prem packaging and upgrade process and will surface compliance evidence.
- Objection: "We rely on a particular cloud or GPU type."
  - Rebuttal: Redwood supports smart routing and kernel selection for major GPU families; for Dedicated/Private we work with your infra team to validate target hardware.

Pitch Deck (recommended slide flow, 10–12 slides):
1) Title + hook (customer logo if permitted)
2) Problem: inference cost, latency, and operational burden in production LLMs
3) Redwood solution overview (1-liner + platform modes)
4) Architecture at a glance (serving runtime, routing, caching)
5) Performance & cost evidence (benchmarks, tokens/sec, p95 latencies)
6) Deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private) + security/compliance summary
7) Developer experience (API, SDKs, rollouts, tracing)
8) Case study snapshot (metrics-focused)
9) Pricing & packaging (high-level tiers and procurement notes)
10) POC plan + success criteria
11) Implementation timeline & ownership
12) CTA & next steps (license terms, trial access, security questionnaire)

Pricing Guidance & Negotiation Levers:
- Pricing tiers (high level):
  - Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing for generation and embeddings, volume tiers that reduce unit price at scale.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commitments for predictable throughput; baseline commit + overage model.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): platform licensing fee + support tier; optional professional services for deployment.
- Example guidance (illustrative, align to Sales Ops numbers per deal):
  - Small pilot: Hosted API with $5k credit for 30 days; target metrics: latency < 200ms p95, baseline throughput for feature tests.
  - Mid-market: Dedicated with 12-month commit; discount tiers at 6–12 month MAUs and token volumes; include 8–12 weeks onboarding + 1 month performance tuning.
  - Enterprise: Private deployment with enterprise license, + professional services for integration, KMS/HSM setup, SOC2 evidence share, and 24x7 support SLA.
- Negotiation levers: commit duration, usage volume tiers, support SLA level, training/professional services, data residency guarantees, and feature prioritization (roadmap influence).

Deal Economics & Typical Metrics to Track:
- Key metrics: monthly tokens, p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, model mix (large vs small), cache hit rate, average batch size.
- Use Redwood Console reports to quantify current vs projected run-rate and cost delta for proposed config. Share a 12‑month TCO comparison when recommending Dedicated vs Hosted.

Case Studies (anonymized summaries):
1) FinTechCo — Personalized Customer Support
- Problem: High latency and high inference costs when serving personalized assistance to customers; recurrent cold-start overheads.
- Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching and quantization profile for mid-size LLM; prefix caching reduced repeated context cost.
- Outcome: 3x reduction in average response cost per session, p95 latency improved from 480ms to 160ms, and model hosting ops headcount reduced by one FTE.

2) HealthAI (Regulated Enterprise) — Clinical Triage Assistant
- Problem: Strict data residency and auditability requirements prevented use of public LLM APIs.
- Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS integration, and audit logging enabled.
- Outcome: Successful SOC2 readiness review, 0 compliance exceptions in the first 6 months, and 2x faster triage throughput enabling the product team to scale features into additional clinics.

POC & Closing Playbook (step-by-step):
1) Qualification: confirm personas, security needs, target throughput, and success metrics (latency, cost, feature coverage).
2) Security intake: complete our security questionnaire and determine if Private/Dedicated is required.
3) POC design: agree on dataset, traffic profile, success criteria, timeline (4–8 weeks typical).
4) Onboarding: sandbox API keys, sample prompts, and Redwood Console access for telemetry.
5) Performance tuning: run perf suite, enable batching/caching, and apply quantization recommendations.
6) Business review: share detailed TCO, performance reports, and recommended production config.
7) Contract & procurement: outline recommended tier, support level, and deployment option.
8) Production rollout: canary → stage → global rollout with tracing hooks and rollback policy.

Demo & POC Checklist (technical):
- Provide SDK quickstart and bring-your-own-model example that matches customer workload.
- Show Console telemetry: token breakdown, end-to-end latency, and model-level dashboards.
- Demonstrate fallback routing and canary rollout in front of traffic.
- Validate KMS integration, audit log ingestion, and RBAC for a sample team.

Security FAQ (prospect-facing, short answers):
Q: What certifications and audits does Redwood have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. We are actively pursuing ISO 27001 and can provide audit artifacts under NDA. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer audit access as contractually defined.

Q: How is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. At rest, we encrypt data using AES-256; for Private/Dedicated deployments customers may provide KMS/HSM keys for envelope encryption.

Q: Can you support data residency requirements?
A: Yes. Hosted customers can be provisioned in regional clusters; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment options which can be hosted in specific cloud regions or on-prem.

Q: How do you handle customer keys and secrets?
A: We offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can support customer-managed keys for encryption and signing. HSM-backed key storage is available for Private deployments.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are available?
A: We provide structured audit logs, request/response metadata (configurable redaction), and integration hooks (SIEM export) for long-term retention. Logs are queryable from the Console for troubleshooting and compliance.

Q: Do you retain prompts or model outputs?
A: By default Redwood retains request metadata and telemetry for operational purposes. Data retention policies are configurable per contract; for high-sensitivity customers we can disable retention and/or route logs to the customer-managed storage.

Q: What does your incident response process look like?
A: We maintain a documented IR plan, 24x7 on-call rotations, and will notify impacted customers per SLA and contractual obligations. Incident postmortems are shared internally; for customers we provide an executive summary and remediation timeline.

Q: Can you provide penetration testing and third-party assessments?
A: Yes. Redwood conducts regular internal and external pen tests and vulnerability scans. We can coordinate on-targeted assessments for enterprise customers and share findings under NDA.

Q: How do you support regulated workloads (HIPAA, PCI, etc.)?
A: Redwood provides Private deployment patterns and contractual terms to support regulated workloads. For HIPAA-level needs we execute Business Associate Agreements and work with customers on deployment architecture and additional controls.

Sales Execution & Artifacts to Share:
- Always share: one-page TL;DR, 10–12 slide pitch deck, anonymized case study PDF, high-level pricing spreadsheet, and the Security FAQ.
- Ask for: security questionnaire, expected traffic profile, and procurement timeline.

Owner & Escalation Matrix:
- Primary GTM owner: AE assigned to opportunity.
- Technical owner: Solutions Engineer (SE) for POC and demo.
- Security escalations: product-security@redwood.ai and Customer Security Engineering (CSE) on rotation.
- Contract/legal: go-to-market-ops@redwood.ai.
